_source: Built from UIT.md (End-of-Pre-Camp Student Diagnostic and Reflection, full question bank) cross-referenced against results-6c0699d6-...csv (the actual export's Q-numbering).
_excluded: Q1/Q2 (consent), Q5 (degree/programme -- branch already covers Q6), and Q48-Q54 (Section H/I/J/K: pre/post mindset-shift battery, session feedback, presenter feedback, bootcamp interest -- a different instrument from the career-readiness diagnostic per UIT.md's own section structure) are left unmapped/raw-context rather than forced into B-G.
_ordinal_design: Sections B-E are self-report 'which statement best describes you' questions with a genuine low->high maturity gradient, so options_low_to_high is filled in. Sections F-G are scenario/best-practice-judgment questions (UIT.md itself says to randomise their option order and hide the correct answer after submission -- i.e. one correct answer plus distractors, not a smooth scale), so ranking the distractors against each other would be guesswork; these are left fully AI-judged from the raw answer text instead, same mechanism as multi-select. A few individual questions (Q8, Q10, Q18) are also non-ordinal/categorical and intentionally left empty -- see the '_note' on each. Trailing not-applicable options (e.g. 'I have not yet had such an experience') are deliberately left OUT of a question's options_low_to_high so they fall back to AI judgment instead of being forced into a maturity position.
_caveat: Option text is transcribed from UIT.md. Exact-match scoring against the live CSV depends on punctuation (curly vs straight apostrophes, en-dashes) matching exactly -- a mismatch just falls back to AI-only judgment for that answer (no crash), so this is a soft risk, not a blocker.

F.label: Coachability & problem-solving approach

questions.correct_answer: Clarify the intended outcome and constraints, state necessary assumptions and begin with a small test.
questions.full_question: You receive an assignment with an incomplete description and an approaching deadline. What would you most likely do first?

questions.correct_answer: Compare their assumptions and evidence, then verify through documentation or testing.
questions.full_question: Two reliable-looking sources provide different explanations for the same technical issue. What would you most likely do?

questions.correct_answer: Record what happened, isolate one possible cause and test it.
questions.full_question: You have attempted the same problem several times and it continues to fail. What would you most likely do next?

questions.correct_answer: Ask for specific feedback, revisit the assumptions and rebuild weak areas where necessary.
questions.full_question: A mentor tells you that your output works, but your understanding and design are weak. What would you most likely do?

questions.correct_answer: Examine the evidence, compare assumptions and test the competing approaches where practical.
questions.full_question: A teammate presents evidence that your preferred design may fail under higher load. What would you do first?

F._note: Scenario/best-practice-judgment questions (see _ordinal_design). Empirically, leaving these with no computed hint at all caused the model to return null instead of scoring the section, so each question is tagged with its single correct_answer (from UIT.md) -- scoring.py turns % of scenario answers matched into a real computed hint (100=all matched, 0=none), same as any other section. The AI still writes the narrative from the raw answers, this only fixes the missing-hint problem.

G.label: Systems & critical thinking

questions.correct_answer: “Quickly” is not defined in measurable terms.
questions.full_question: A requirement states: “The application should respond quickly.” What is the main problem with this requirement?

questions.correct_answer: Which students are affected, and what specifically are they unhappy about?
questions.full_question: A stakeholder says, “Students are unhappy with the portal.” What is the best first question?

questions.correct_answer: The software update caused the complaints.
questions.full_question: A report states: “Complaints increased after the latest software update.” Which conclusion is not justified by that statement alone?

questions.correct_answer: The available information is insufficient; evidence from multiple layers is required.
questions.full_question: A user taps a button and sees: “Something went wrong. Please try again.” What is the most responsible technical conclusion?

questions.correct_answer: Algorithmic complexity, database load or shared-resource contention
questions.full_question: A system works well for 20 users but becomes slow when 1,000 users access it simultaneously. Which factor should be investigated first?

questions.correct_answer: Data may accumulate, be overwritten or be lost unless buffering and flow control are designed.
questions.full_question: A sensor sends one reading every second, but the receiving system processes only one reading per minute. What is the most likely concern?

questions.correct_answer: One component depends on the other component’s internal data format and implementation details.
questions.full_question: Which situation demonstrates strong coupling between two components?

questions.correct_answer: Decide based on failure impact, budget, reliability requirements and recovery options.
questions.full_question: A team has two possible designs. Design A: lower cost, but one component failure can stop the entire system. Design B: higher cost, but the system continues operating after one component fails. How should the team choose?

questions.correct_answer: The code works under that tested condition, but wider validation is still required.
questions.full_question: AI generates code that passes one demonstration test. What can the team reasonably conclude?

questions.correct_answer: Prioritise using impact, risk, dependencies and effort.
questions.full_question: A team has limited time and money to address ten known system problems. What is the best way to decide the order?

questions.correct_answer: Its expected impact may still be high because the consequence is severe.
questions.full_question: A software defect occurs only once a year but can cause major financial or safety consequences. Why might it still deserve high priority?

questions.correct_answer: Improve alert thresholds, add context and verify high-risk cases.
questions.full_question: A monitoring system produces many alerts, but only a small percentage correspond to real failures. What is the best improvement?

G._note: Scenario/best-practice-judgment questions. UIT.md itself says to randomise option order and hide the correct answer, confirming this is a right/wrong assessment. Each question is tagged with its correct_answer (from UIT.md) so scoring.py can compute a real hint (see F's _note for why this was necessary) -- the AI still writes the narrative from the raw answers, correctness just anchors the numeric score instead of the AI having to invent one from nothing.
